purpose: Fix the exact completion, failure and evidence criteria for Step 2 before any V2 executable artifact is written.

scopeBoundary.step2Means: A source-bound, deterministic, schema-valid and fixture-qualified V2 executable contract, simulator, result chain, migration chain and executable seal that are ready for Step 3 large-scale validation.
step2DoesNotMean: Economy, gacha tails or long-horizon balance are approved.
Runtime, backend, payments or ads are implemented.
Vercel READY or a successful command alone proves product quality.
allowed: V2 candidate, schemas, validators, deterministic engine, run plan, result chain, fixtures, migrations, dedicated Step 2 workflow, quality evidence and status mirrors
Small deterministic qualification runs required to prove the executable chain
forbidden: PR, branch creation, merge, rebase, cherry-pick or force-push
Step 3 large-scale balance execution or PASS claim before the Step 2 seal is active

acceptanceCriteria.requirement: All V2 artifacts bind the exact active Step 1 seal, authoritative source blobs and this Acceptance blob/commit; any digest mismatch fails closed.
Every write explicitly targets existing kimi; no other branch, PR, Production alias, runtime, assets, backend or provider path changes.
V1 remains byte-identical and cannot be used, extended or promoted by the V2 validators, workflow or seal.
candidate-v2 and result-v2 pass strict JSON Schema validation with unknown fields rejected in closed contract objects.
Cross-field validation covers every required invariant, registered ID, probability sum, unit, authority boundary, recovery path and dependency presence.
Missing engine, schema, fixture, migration, run-plan, result-validator, digest or seal dependency is rejected; no warning-only promotion path exists.
Canonical arbitrary-precision decimal serialization rejects unsafe integers, NaN, Infinity, implicit exponent persistence, locale parsing and unversioned rounding.
Node golden fixtures cover ordering, add, subtract-underflow policy, multiply, divide, floor, ceil, half-even, serialization, very-large floors and display/internal separation.
Canonical IDs and generated tower IDs obey minimum-width/overflow rules; aliases, alternate leading-zero canonical writes and unknown IDs are rejected.
No visible floor cap exists; fixtures cover 1, 5, 10, 100, 101, 1000, 10000 and a very-large decimal floor with deterministic district/cycle/boss/modifier generation.
Only reset.tower_return exists; Floor 1 restart, complete quote/commit losses-retention, first effective reset target configuration and repeat-best zero-ruby are executable and fixture-tested.
Uncapped coin levels, 100-level evolution eligibility, non-blocking level continuation, ordered catch-up and first-reset-funded first evolution are enforced.
N/R deterministic acquisition and core-role coverage are machine-checkable; no specific RR-UR is a core progression gate.

Character and weapon pools are separated; exact rates sum correctly; 99/100 hard pity, 199/200 featured guarantee, compatible carryover, exchange, history and expired-banner behavior are fixture-tested.
First copy is functionally complete, practical breakpoints precede 20+ long-term full mastery, marginal gains diminish and post-cap overflow has a deterministic non-loss path.
Paid/free ruby provenance, configured consumption order, conservation and non-expiring paid ruby are enforced; spent-paid-ruby refund creates explicit deficit/restriction without free-ledger debit.
Payment, rewarded ad, login, reset, evolution, mastery exchange, account link and deletion machines cover idempotency, retry, replay, multi-tab, out-of-order and recovery states.
Rewarded opt-in ads and login claims bind immutable catalog/version, use server authority/time, enforce exactly-once grants and test stale, duplicate, cap and rollover cases.
The same candidate, seed, algorithm, rounding and scenario identity produce byte-identical normalized result hashes across repeated Node runs.
run-plan-v2 defines 3 builds x 5 personas x at least 1000 seeds, all required horizons and separate high-volume suites, while marking full execution as Step 3 work.
Calibration and holdout seed namespaces are disjoint, generated from committed rules, not copied from observed V1 results and not both exposed to tuning outputs.
Every invariant and required field family has a negative fixture; all required positive, boundary, state, migration and cross-runtime fixtures are present and manifest-bound.
V1-to-V2 migration is idempotent, preserves immutable raw backup and provenance, canonicalizes aliases only on output, merges Dawn into reset.tower_return and fails closed on ownership conflict.
A small Step 2 qualification run validates the complete executable chain without making Step 3 balance claims; results pass result-v2 validation and reproduce by recorded commands.
A dedicated Step 2 workflow or equivalent committed verification entrypoint checks source digests, candidate, result, fixtures, migrations and seal; historical workflows cannot promote V2.
At least five independent critic perspectives cover product semantics, numeric/determinism, economy/probability, state-machine/security and repository/governance; all P0/P1 are resolved and rerun.
The executable seal binds exact source, acceptance, candidate, schema, validator, engine, fixtures, migrations, run-plan, result-validator, qualification-result and critic/final-judge digests.
Completion evidence and a later live branch read-back bind content commit, evidence commit, final tree, seal ancestry, unchanged forbidden paths, Step 2 PASS and Step 3 READY_TO_START.

passOnlyWhen: All required artifacts exist and their committed digests match the executable seal.
All qualification commands exit zero and negative fixtures fail for the expected reason.
Independent critics and final judge report zero unresolved P0 and P1.
A direct-descendant completion evidence commit and later live read-back confirm Step 2 PASS and Step 3 READY_TO_START.
No forbidden path or external/Production operation occurred.
